name: KY-027 magic light cup module (tilt switch + LED)
description: A mercury tilt switch and a 5 mm LED on one board, sold in pairs for the 'pouring light' trick. The switch sits between S and G with a 10 kOhm pull-up from S to +, so S is HIGH while the switch is open and LOW while the mercury closes it (which tilt closes it depends on how you hold the board). The LED is wired from L (anode) to G with NO series resistor on the board: add 120 Ohm at 3.3 V or 220 Ohm at 5 V. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: Keyes KY-027 / HW-499 magic light cup module (black 4-pin sensor-kit board with glass mercury switch, 10k resistor R1 and LED LD1; header G, +, S, L).
eli5: A tilt switch and a little light on one board. Your program can tell when the board is tipped and turn the light on or fade it.

pins.name: G
pins.description: Ground: return for the tilt switch and the LED cathode
Supply for the 10 kOhm pull-up on S, 3.3-5 V. Use 3V3 with an ESP32 or Pico, because S is pulled up to this voltage.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Tilt switch output: HIGH while the switch is open, LOW while the mercury closes it to G

pins.name: L
pins.description: LED anode: HIGH (or PWM) lights the LED. No resistor on the board: fit 120 Ohm (3.3 V) or 220 Ohm (5 V) in series

buildNotes: Header order as printed: G, +, S, L.
Put a 120 Ohm resistor (3.3 V GPIO) or 220 Ohm (5 V) between the GPIO and L: the board has no LED resistor, and wiring a GPIO straight to L overloads the LED and the pin.
On an ESP32 or Pico connect + to 3V3: the on-board 10 kOhm pull-up takes S to the + voltage, so 5 V on + puts 5 V on the GPIO.
S is LOW while the switch is closed and HIGH while it is open. Which tilt closes it depends on how the board is held; invert in code if needed.
The mercury bead bounces at each change; debounce for about 50 ms (the driver's closed() does this).
Drive L from a PWM-capable pin if you want to fade the LED (the 'pouring light' effect with two modules).
The switch contains mercury: do not break the glass, and dispose of a damaged board as hazardous waste.

driver.code:
# KY-027 magic light cup module, MicroPython driver.
# The board carries two independent circuits on a 4-pin header G, +, S, L:
#  * a mercury tilt switch between S and G (GND) with a 10 kOhm pull-up (marked 103)
#    from S to +. S is HIGH while the switch is open and LOW while the mercury
#    bridges the contacts. Which tilt closes it depends on how the board is held.
#  * an LED whose anode is L and whose cathode is G. There is NO series resistor on
#    the board: put 120 Ohm (3.3 V) or 220 Ohm (5 V) between the GPIO and L.
# Power + from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board: the pull-up takes S up to the + supply.
from machine import Pin, PWM
import time


class KY027:
    def __init__(self, s_pin, l_pin, debounce_ms=50):
        # The board has its own 10k pull-up; an internal pull-up is harmless and
        # keeps S defined if + is left unconnected.
        self.s = Pin(s_pin, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP)
        self.l_num = l_pin
        self.l = Pin(l_pin, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self._pwm = None
        self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms

    def raw(self):
        """Logic level on S right now: 0 = switch closed, 1 = open."""
        return self.s.value()

    def closed(self):
        """Debounced: True if S stays LOW (switch closed) for debounce_ms."""
        state = self.s.value()
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < self.debounce_ms:
            v = self.s.value()
            if v != state:
                state = v
                t0 = time.ticks_ms()
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        return state == 0

    def led(self, on):
        """Switch the LED fully on or off."""
        if self._pwm is not None:
            self._pwm.deinit()
            self._pwm = None
            self.l = Pin(self.l_num, Pin.OUT)
        self.l.value(1 if on else 0)

    def brightness(self, level, freq=1000):
        """Dim the LED with PWM: level 0..255 (the 'pouring light' effect)."""
        level = max(0, min(255, int(level)))
        if self._pwm is None:
            self._pwm = PWM(Pin(self.l_num), freq=freq)
        self._pwm.duty_u16(level * 65535 // 255)

example.code:
from ky027 import KY027
import time

# 120 Ohm resistor between the GPIO and L (no LED resistor on the board).
cup = KY027({S}, {L})
while True:
    c = cup.closed()
    cup.led(c)
    print('Switch: %s' % ('closed' if c else 'open'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
